plan.title: Genotype x drug interaction in KO vs WT heart RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is an interaction question: does the drug effect differ between KO and WT? The inputs are a 12,000 x 17 CSV of raw integer gene-level Salmon counts (first column gene symbol, 16 sample columns) and a 16 x 4 sample table carrying genotype (WT, KO), treatment (vehicle, drug) and condition, human heart tissue, 4 replicates per each of the 4 cells. The plan therefore fits one negative-binomial model with the design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, with WT and vehicle set as explicit reference levels, and reads the interaction coefficient (drug-vs-vehicle in KO minus drug-vs-vehicle in WT) as the primary answer. Because an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error, at 4 replicates per cell it is the least powerful test in the design; the plan therefore always reports the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, drug vs vehicle within KO) beside the interaction, and states the power caveat rather than letting a short interaction list read as an absence of differential drug action. Every script is Python per the user constraint: pydeseq2 replaces DESeq2 and gseapy replaces fgsea; there is no R step in the plan. T1S1 does sample-structure QC (blind variance-stabilising-style transform, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) so that an outlier sample or a cell that does not separate is known before the model. T1S2 fits the model and produces all contrasts with ashr-style shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold changes, BH adjustment within contrast at alpha 0.05, and p-value histograms. T1S3 is a robustness cross-check of the interaction call with an independent Python implementation (statsmodels NB GLM likelihood-ratio test of the interaction term), reporting the overlap rather than the union. T2S1 runs preranked GSEA per contrast on the Wald statistic (the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics) against the human hallmark collection and a second human canonical-pathway collection. T1S4 assembles the report. Note: the counts arrive as a gene-symbol matrix, not as Salmon transcript output, so the tximport length-offset route is not available in this environment; the step must state that the length offset could not be applied and that a fold change driven purely by isoform-length shift cannot be excluded.

steps.description: For each of the three contrasts (interaction, drug-vs-vehicle in WT, drug-vs-vehicle in KO) build a ranked list of every tested gene by the Wald statistic — this is the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties. Run gseapy preranked GSEA with a fixed random seed against the human hallmark gene set collection first, then against a second human canonical-pathway collection (Reactome is the preferred second collection; if the staged canonical-pathway resource covers KEGG MEDICUS / BioCarta / PID rather than Reactome, use that and name exactly which collection and version was used). Restrict sets to 15–500 genes after intersecting with the tested genes. Apply BH within each contrast and collection. Collapse redundant significant sets by leading-edge overlap and report one representative per group with the full table as supplement. Report the share of ranked genes not found in the collection. Run each contrast separately and never pool genes across contrasts. Do not run an over-representation test on a thresholded list; if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj < 0.05 in a contrast, state that and rely on the ranked result.
acceptance_criteria: Three separate GSEA result tables, one per contrast, each labelled with its contrast name — no pooling across contrasts
Ranking metric recorded as the Wald statistic, with the choice stated in the output
Gene set collection names and versions recorded for both passes, resolved from what the environment actually holds
Set size window 15–500 applied after intersection with the tested genes and reported
Leading-edge genes listed for each significant set, with redundant sets collapsed by leading-edge overlap and a representative reported
Share of ranked genes unmatched to the collection reported
Random seed set and recorded
Number of genes passing padj < 0.05 per contrast stated alongside the ranked results
constraints: Python only — gseapy prerank, not fgsea in R
Rank the FULL list of tested genes; never cut the list by padj or fold change before GSEA
rank_metric = Wald statistic (stat); do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone or by a signed p-value with ties
min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome
One enrichment run per contrast; BH within contrast and within collection
Human gene sets only — the data are Homo sapiens heart; a mouse collection would silently match almost nothing
State the collection and its version in the output; use only locally staged collections, no network downloads
caveats: If the interaction contrast yields few or no significant sets, that is a genuine possible answer at this sample size — report it as such rather than switching to a laxer threshold
Enrichment results are method-dependent; a set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment on count data; the tested-gene universe removes only part of that bias

grounding.reason: Ranked enrichment on the full tested list is the default (R-0107); human hallmark first then a second canonical-pathway collection (R-0048, R-0098); disputed ranking metric R-0108 resolved in favour of the Wald statistic, stated here; run once per contrast (R-0104). Symbols are already the collection identifier space, so the Entrez remapping of R-0101 is not needed.

steps.name: Integrated interaction report
steps.question: Taken together, does the drug act differently in the knockout than in the wild type in human heart, and how strong is the evidence given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.context: Assembles T1S2 (model and contrasts), T1S3 (cross-check) and T2S1 (enrichment) into one answer to the research question, with the power limitation stated up front rather than buried.
steps.description: Build a single report. Lead with the direct answer: the number of genes with a significant genotype:treatment interaction at padj < 0.05, and whether that supports a genotype-dependent drug effect. For every gene in the interaction set, present the three quantities side by side: drug-vs-vehicle log2FC in WT, drug-vs-vehicle log2FC in KO, and the interaction contrast, each with its lfcSE and padj, plus both shrunken and unshrunken fold changes. Name the reference levels (WT, vehicle) beside the table because every coefficient's meaning depends on them. Include the MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms from T1S2; the intersection and method-exclusive counts from T1S3; and the per-contrast enrichment tables with leading-edge genes from T2S1. Add plots of normalised counts for the top interaction genes across all four cells, so the reader can see the crossing or diverging pattern directly. Record the reproducibility block: package versions, random seeds, gene set collection names and versions, design formula, contrasts, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, number of DE genes per contrast. State the power caveat for the interaction test and the missing transcript-length offset.
acceptance_criteria: Report leads with the interaction gene count at padj < 0.05 and a plain statement of whether the drug effect differs by genotype
Per-gene table gives the WT simple effect, the KO simple effect and the interaction contrast side by side with lfcSE and padj for each
Reference levels WT and vehicle named beside every table
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms included with a one-line reading of each
Normalised-count plots across all four genotype x treatment cells for the top interaction genes
Two-method overlap from T1S3 reported as a count with the intersection named as the high-confidence set
Enrichment section names the collection, its version, the Wald-statistic ranking metric, the tested-gene universe and the 15–500 size window, and lists leading-edge genes per reported set
Reproducibility record present: package versions, seeds, collection versions, design, thresholds, n tested, n DE per contrast
The low power of an interaction test at 4 replicates per cell is stated explicitly, as is the absence of the transcript-length offset
constraints: Python only for every figure and table
Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not interpret a significant simple effect in one genotype plus a non-significant one in the other as an interaction
State that enrichment results are method-dependent and are hypotheses for follow-up
Do not overstate: if the interaction set is empty or tiny, say so and do not substitute the simple effects as the answer to the interaction question
caveats: A null interaction result at this sample size is under-powered, not proof of equivalence — do not phrase it as 'the drug acts identically'
This is one tissue at one timepoint with n=4 per cell; nothing here establishes mechanism

grounding.reason: Interaction design reporting: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side with named reference levels (R-0092), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051, R-0105), and a full reproducibility record (R-0086, R-0041).
